newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition puts off decision on leader.
newsitem.headline: India coalition puts off decision on leader.

text.p: India's search for a new leader to end a 19-day political crisis was delayed on Thursday, but the ousted United Front coalition said it was confident a new prime minister would take power in the next few days. The 15-party alliance postponed a decision on who would replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda due to political infighting and the death of a veteran party boss, coalition leaders said.

The United Front's policy-making Steering Committee met on Thursday afternoon but quickly adjourned after paying its respects to veteran politician Biju Patnaik, who died earlier in the day in a New Delhi hospital.
Patnaik, former chief minister of the eastern Indian state of Orissa, died on Thursday in a New Delhi hospital, United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said.
Regional party chief G.K. Moopanar, considered a frontrunner to succeed Deve Gowda, said the coalition would tap a new leader on Friday at a meeting due to start at 10 a.m. (0430 GMT).
"The Steering Committee will decide on it tomorrow," he said.

Patnaik, who was 81, was a senior leader of Deve Gowda's Janata Dal, the biggest single unit in the 15-party United Front coalition with 45 seats in the lower house of parliament. The front has 178 votes in the 542-member house, the Lok Sabha. Deve Gowda resigned last Friday after losing a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha by a lopsided margin.

His downfall was precipitated by the Congress party, which had shored up Deve Gowda's minority coalition for 10 months but abruptly withdrew its backing on March 30, accusing the alliance of trying to sideline India's oldest party.
However, the United Front and Congress, fearing a return to power by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), have since agreed to try to sink their differences.
Congress said on Monday it would support a new government led by the same alliance provided the United Front replaced Deve Gowda.
The Steering Committee had been expected to choose a new leader at its meeting on Thursday, but the decision was put off.
United Front officials said the decision was delayed in part because of a demand by left-wing parties that Congress first withdraw a letter staking a claim to power.

Congress has said withdrawal of the letter would be a formality once the United Front selects a new chief. But the four left-wing parties in the alliance, including India's two main communist groups, said on Wednesday they would insist that Congress move first.
The Left Front fears Congress could make an eventual push for power if the United Front stumbled in its own efforts.
Politicians also acknowledged that the United Front needed more time to sift through a growing list of contenders to succeed Deve Gowda.
Asked when a new government might be formed, United Front spokesman Reddy said: "I believe by the 20th."
Parliament was set next Monday to take up the government budget, which sent share prices soaring when it was presented in February but has been held hostage by the political crisis.
